requirement: The bundled skills MUST direct agents to make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows; to use `{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole; and to mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed requirement that its sites do not uphold.
rationale:
The subject requires the bundled skills to direct agents to do three things:
1. Make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of many sites.
2. Use `{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole.
3. Mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed requirement that its sites do not uphold.

The only test is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_make_a_requirement_distributed_only_for_per_site_obligations]`. It reads the "## Do" section of the habeas skill's `references/distributed-requirements.md`. It does this through the `distributed_reference()` and `section()` helpers. It then uses `assert_text` to require two exact guidance bullets:
- "Make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each site; when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole, use `{impl}` there." This covers obligations 1 and 2, including the "only when" restriction and the contrast with `{impl}`.
- "Separate obligations each site upholds from obligations particular code carries out, and mark that code `{impl}`." This covers obligation 3, the split between site-upheld obligations and obligations that need `{impl}` on particular code.

I read the guidance file, `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md`. The "## Do" section contains both bullets. The "such as a convention every validation function follows" example appears in the file's intro. The subject uses it only as an illustration ("such as"), so it is not a separate obligation.

The assertions are scoped to the right section, so the phrases can't be satisfied by text elsewhere in the file. `assert_text` panics on any missing phrase, so removing or weakening either bullet would fail the test. I found no input class or mode the text distinguishes that the test leaves uncovered. Other tests cover related requirements such as the do/don't list format and the bootstrap skill. They are not needed for this subject.
